description: Question: what does "heart-rate variability" measure, and why does every HRV standard insist on normal-to-normal (NN) intervals? Idea: HRV is computed from beat times alone. PhysioNet's LightWAVE server gives the cardiologists' beat annotations of three Holter records (first 15 minutes each, so the windows are alike): a healthy 32-year-old (NSR database 16265, 128 Hz), MIT-BIH 100 (sinus rhythm with a few premature atrial beats) and MIT-BIH 119 (ventricular bigeminy, 360 Hz). Polars turns them into RR intervals, marks the NN ones (both beats normal, 300–2000 ms) and computes the time-domain measures of the 1996 ESC/NASPE Task Force: SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50, and the Poincaré plot's SD1 (beat-to-beat, = RMSSD/√2, checked in the table) and SD2 (slow). Aha: the healthy heart is irregular in a structured way (SD1 21 ms across a long comet of SD2 121 ms, SD1/SD2 = 0.18), while ectopic beats fake variability: in 119 the 197 premature ventricular beats make RMSSD 437 ms from every beat against 36 ms from NN intervals (12×, pNN50 62% against 17%); and even in the healthy record one 6.6-second stretch the annotators marked as noise becomes a single 6,617 ms "interval" that multiplies RMSSD by 7.7. The PVCs also show the full compensatory pause: coupling 536 ms + pause 1,311 ms ≈ 2 × the 900 ms NN interval (median ratio 1.03), because the early ventricular beat doesn't reset the sinus node. A 12-second ECG trace of 119 (lead MLII; LightWAVE sends samples delta-coded, so a cumulative sum and (adu − 1024)/200 give mV) shows where each interval comes from. Caveats: three people, 15-minute windows (SDNN grows with window length; compare like with like), different sampling rates (128 Hz gives ±8 ms beat-time resolution, which inflates RMSSD a little), annotations by cardiologists rather than a beat detector, HRV depends strongly on age, heart rate, posture and breathing, and no frequency-domain HRV (LF/HF needs a spectrum of the resampled tachogram, which Polars can't do). Data: PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000), MIT-BIH Arrhythmia and Normal Sinus Rhythm databases, Open Data Commons Attribution 1.0. Next: the other 46 MIT-BIH records, the full 24 h of nsrdb in 15-minute windows (circadian HRV), detrended fluctuation or sample entropy, and the spectrum with a Python step.
name: Heart-rate variability from ECG beats
